# Hippius

> Hippius is a distributed cloud: encrypted file storage (Drive), S3-compatible object storage, a registry for AI models and containers (Hub), and confidential compute (VMs, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes, GitHub Actions runners). One account pays for all of them. This file says what each product is and which file to open next.

Open only the file for the product you need. The long reference for the whole product, including the S3 manual, is [llms-full.txt](https://docs.hippius.com/llms-full.txt)

## Which file to open

| Want to | Open |
|---|---|
| Store or fetch files from code, rclone, or a backup tool | [hippius-s3 llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-s3/staging/llms.txt) |
| Store encrypted files in the browser (Drive) | [Drive guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/drive) |
| Publish or pull a model or a container image | [hippius-hub llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-hub/main/llms.txt) |
| Sync folders on a computer | [hippius-desktop llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-desktop/staging/llms.txt) |
| Work in a shared drive | A Drive someone else owns and invited you into. They pay for the storage. It shows in the console under Storage after the invite. |
| Give a coding agent shared memory | [hippius-mem llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-mem/main/llms.txt) |
| Script Drive with encryption on the client | [hippius-drive-sdk llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-drive-sdk/main/llms.txt) |
| Sign up, pay, get an API token, or manage Drive and S3 keys in the browser | [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started) |
| Use Drive on an Android phone | [Mobile getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/mobile/getting-started) |
| Run a VM, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes or GitHub Actions runners (Compute) | [Compute guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute) |
| Serve an S3 bucket through the CDN (zones on <zone>.c.hipcdn.net or your own domain; FR $0.010/GB, AU $0.060/GB, $0.002 per 10,000 requests, $1/month per custom domain) | [CDN guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn) |
| Filter requests to a CDN zone with a WAF: custom rules, rate limits, IP/ASN/country lists (private beta; Standard $5, Advanced $20 per zone per month) | [CDN guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn) |
| Read compute, CDN, S3, Drive and Hub prices without an account (GET https://api.hippius.com/api/compute/public-prices/, no auth), or sign users in with their 12-word access key from your own app | [Management API](https://docs.hippius.com/use/api), which links the Public Price API and Access Key Sign-In API pages |
| Let team members use your compute, S3 and CDN, or work in an account you were invited to (shared accounts) | [Shared accounts guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team) |
| Run a storage miner | [Miner guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/arion/running-miner) and [arion llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/arion/main/llms.txt) |
| Run a validator | [Validator guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/installing-validator) |

## Account, sign-in, and paying

Full console guide: [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started)
Billing: [Billing guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing)

- One account covers the console, the desktop app, and the mobile app. Sign-in is Google, GitHub, Apple, or an existing 12-word access key. There is no email and password sign-in.
- An agent cannot create the account or sign in. That happens in the user's browser or app.
- A 12-word access key creates a wallet-only account. It has no real email address, so it gets no lifecycle mail. Drive has no free plan: subscribe before the first upload. S3 and Hub work the same as on any other account.
- S3 endpoint is https://s3.hippius.com only. Keys (the access key id starts with `hip_`) are created on the console S3 page: https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/s3
- The API token for Hub and the account API is on console Settings: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/settings
- Hub has a second credential, the registry robot login, created when the namespace is provisioned.
- Drive encryption uses an unlock password and a 12-word recovery seed. Never ask the user to paste either into chat.
- 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. Topping up fills the balance. It does not add storage. Subscribe to a plan for that. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- Top up on Billing in one of five ways. Card, through Stripe, from $10 to $10,000, or a monthly auto reload. Bitcoin, on-chain or Lightning, from $20 to $100,000. Lightning lands in seconds; on-chain after one confirmation. USDC on Base from a browser wallet, from $5 to $10,000; 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. TAO, from a connected wallet or by sending to the TAO deposit address (Manually tab), at least $20 per transfer; never send TAO to the Hippius account address, which is not credited. A transfer cannot be reversed. hAlpha (Hippius native token), on the Hippius tab: credits = hAlpha × the on-chain hAlpha price, 1% slippage protection by default, final on chain with no refund. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- An agent with enough balance subscribes without a browser. Auth: `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN`. Drive: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/drive/subscription/ with `{"plan":"solo","period":"monthly","payment":"credits"}`. Codes `solo` (Starter), `duo` (Plus), `max`, `scale`. S3: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/s3/subscription/ with `{"plan":"pro","rail":"credits"}`. Codes `pro`, `business`, `enterprise`. Hub: GET https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/plans/ then POST https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/subscribe/ with `{"plan_id": 2}` (Builder is id 2; names Free, Builder, Pro, Team). The API requires `plan_id`, not a name. JSON values `credits` mean pay from the existing balance. 201 if the balance covers the plan. Card checkout is a browser; do not send a funded agent there.
- Google, GitHub, and Apple accounts include the Free Drive Plan (10 GB). S3 starts on pay as you go at $6 per TB per month, and a plan is optional.
- Plan prices, monthly, from the balance (always current in the no-auth catalogs: GET https://api.hippius.com/api/drive/plans/ · /api/s3/plans/ · /api/registry/plans/): Drive Free 10 GB $0, Starter 500 GB $4, Plus 2 TB $7, Max 10 TB $22, Scale 25 TB $50 (Max and Scale bill storage above the plan hourly, $2.20 and $2.00 per TB per month, up to a storage cap that defaults to twice the plan). S3 Pro 10 TB $53, Business 50 TB $245, Enterprise 100 TB $465 (pay as you go otherwise: $6 per TB per month). Hub Free $0, Builder $5, Pro $19, Team $99.
- Shared accounts: an owner invites members by email, with Viewer, Operator or Admin access per product (VMs, databases, Kubernetes, runners, S3, CDN). The owner pays and the owner's quotas apply. Drive is not included. With the API, act in another account with the header `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` (ids from GET https://api.hippius.com/api/accounts/). https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team
- Open a support ticket with the account API token: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/support/tickets/ with subject, priority, category, and description.

Hub Free plan: creating a namespace requires a balance of at least $10, a spam check. A zero balance is refused. The plan price stays zero. Top up, then provision. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/hub

## Deprecated

`hipc`, `hippius-cli`, `homebrew-tap`, `hippius-sdk`, `hippius-sdk-ts`, `hippius-sdk-rust`, `hippius-rust-sdk`, `hippius-sync-engine`, `hippius-storage-miner`, and anything else IPFS-related, are deprecated. Hippius switched from IPFS to Arion. https://docs.hippius.com/cli/usage

Chain registration still installs the Python package `hippius`: https://docs.hippius.com/earn/register-in-blockchain

## Compute

Confidential VMs on AMD SEV-SNP, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes and GitHub Actions runners, open to every account. Metered per second (one-minute minimum per VM and public IPv4), charged hourly on the Hippius chain from the account balance. A VM is billed running or stopped until it is deleted. A launch needs a balance covering 24 hours of the account's compute plus the launch, and quotas apply: new accounts start on the Starter tier and move up automatically with their charged usage.

Prices per 730-hour month, on the default NVMe OS disk: vCPU $18, memory $2.50/GB, disk $0.10/GB. Small (1 vCPU, 4 GB, 40 GB) is $32 a month ($0.0438/h), Medium $64, Large $128, X-Large $256, 2X-Large $512, 4X-Large $1024. The OS disk tier is chosen at launch and fixed: SSD (disk $0.06/GB, Small $27.60, Medium $55.20, Large $110.40) or HDD, a slow tier for dev and test offered up to Large (disk $0.03/GB, Small $17.16, Medium $34.32, Large $68.64). Dedicated disks (whole physical disks for one VM, up to 8, at least 1,000 GiB each; the VM is then pinned: no backups, migration or failover): $2.50 HDD, $5 SSD, $8 NVMe per TiB-month. Public IPv4 $0.005/h (~$3.65/month). VM backups $6 per TB-month. Outbound bandwidth is metered per region and not charged today; inbound is free. Managed databases cost their VMs plus 25%; Kubernetes costs its VMs plus $15 per cluster per month. The live price list wins: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/billing/compute#prices

- Overview (quotas, the 24-hour balance requirement, billing): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute
- Create a VM and connect over SSH or from the browser: https://docs.hippius.com/use/virtual-machines
- Public IPv4, firewall rules and published ports: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/networking
- Resize a VM (vCPU and memory; the disk is kept): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/resize
- VM backups and restore: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-backups
- Dedicated disks (whole physical HDD/SSD/NVMe disks, exact tier, pinned VM, own quota): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/dedicated-disks
- VM failover: if a VM's server dies, the VM restarts on another server in the same region from its latest backup, keeping its IP and NetBird address; data since that backup is lost. Automatic failover is opt-in per VM, at creation (switch under Automatic backups; API `"failover_mode": "auto"` with `backup_interval_s`) or later in the Backups panel. Offered in France only today. Active after the first full backup: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover
- Placement groups: VMs of one account in the same group (`placement_group` at creation, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, -) are never on the same server. A different server is not a different datacenter. Fixed at creation: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover#placement-groups
- Compute API: base https://api.hippius.com/api, header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN` (plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account). Full OpenAPI spec: https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Create a VM with POST /api/compute/vms/ `{"name":"web-1","flavor":"small","region":"FR","ssh_key_ids":[123]}` (keys from GET /api/ssh-keys/), then poll GET /api/compute/vms/<vm_id>/ until `status` is `running` and, with a public IPv4, `network_ready` is `true`, then SSH to the public IP (or to `netbird_ip` over NetBird). `status` is the lifecycle (billed while `running`, stopped included), `power_state` is on/off. Send your own User-Agent: some default ones (Python urllib) are blocked with 403 error 1010: https://docs.hippius.com/use/api#compute-api
- Managed PostgreSQL 16/17/18 (one-time credentials, TLS, backups to your S3, restore, HA failover): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/databases
- Managed Kubernetes clusters (cluster key, kubeconfig, API access): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes
- Kubernetes worker pools and signed node operations: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-worker-pools
- Kubernetes backups (etcd snapshots, Velero, restore with rclone): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-backups
- GitHub Actions runners (`runs-on: hippius-small|medium|large`): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/runners
- Compute prices, management fees, quotas and unpaid balance: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/billing
- Refusals and troubleshooting: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/troubleshooting

The Kubernetes cluster key is generated in the user's browser, and database credentials are returned once at creation; never ask the user to paste either into chat.
